scenes.text: Can a remote village govern itself better than leaders sitting in New Delhi?
scenes.narration: Imagine if every decision about your local roads, schools, and water came from thousands of kilometers away. Wouldn't the people living in the village solve their daily problems best?

scenes.text: A classroom managing its own homework chart instead of waiting for the school principal.
scenes.narration: Here is a simple analogy: imagine your principal tried to assign daily monitors for forty different classrooms. Wouldn't you prefer letting each class elect someone who sits with them?

scenes.heading: Evolution of Panchayati Raj

events.what: Nehru launches Panchayati Raj at Nagaur
Stagnation from hostile bureaucracy and centralisation

scenes.narration: After early enthusiasm in Nagaur, local councils stagnated for decades because state leaders and bureaucrats resisted sharing power. Finally, the landmark 73rd Amendment in 1992 gave them constitutional recognition.

scenes.heading: Three-Tier Panchayati Raj Structure
scenes.narration: The Balvantray Mehta Committee recommended a uniform three-tier ladder. District and block bodies coordinate planning and resources, while elected village councils implement everyday development on the ground.

scenes.heading: 73rd Amendment: Strengths and Weaknesses

columns.title: Strengths
items: Reserved seats for Dalits and women

scenes.narration: Scholars call the amendment a half-baked cake because it created an institutional skeleton without guaranteed powers. While regular elections and reservations became mandatory, actual funds and functions were left to state discretion.

scenes.heading: Gram Sabha and Direct Democracy
items: All adult village voters form the Gram Sabha
Operates as an organ of direct democracy
Mandated to monitor social audits and spending
Infrequent and bogus meetings weaken accountability
scenes.narration: The Gram Sabha is the soul of grassroots democracy, where every adult voter participates directly rather than through representatives. However, meetings are often irregular, leaving villagers without real control over village funds.

items: 73rd Amendment gave constitutional status to three-tier panchayats
States must devolve funds, functions, and functionaries
Active Gram Sabhas enable genuine direct democracy
scenes.narration: Remember three key lessons: the 73rd Amendment established a uniform three-tier system, real decentralization requires devolving genuine funds and functions, and an active Gram Sabha transforms democracy from paper into reality.
